Where I got to
I reconstructed the full tree from dump.txt (334 files, SHA-256 verified — only export.sh mismatches, because it contains the dump's own # FILE: separator inside itself and the splitter cuts there; I don't touch that file).

First, good news from your terminal logs: Slice 34 is fully green. claude-terminal.txt shows 1078 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 16/16 E2E scenarios, all 8 ci_local.sh gates passing, boot smoke clean. So both Slice 33 and Slice 34 landed. Slice 34's prediction was 1077 — the observed 1078 is one higher, which I'll reconcile in the write-up rather than let stand as a silent discrepancy.

What Slice 35 turned out to be
I went at Slice 34's "Still open" list and the remaining Stage 1b surfaces, and found two findings.

F-68 — the palette is written back into the tree as literals, and two of the copies had drifted.

Full inventory: 95 colour literals outside :root. Of the 45 bare ones:

20 are byte-identical to a declared property — 
#ffffff (=--surface-raised) six times including three in app.css itself, 
#b45309 (=--caution-ink) five, 
#1e7a37 (=--ok-ink) two, 
#7f1d1d (=--danger-ink) two, 
#e6f4ea (=--ok-surface) one, plus rgba(22, 32, 43, α) three times — which is --ink in decimal, the one form no scan for #hex could ever have seen — and rgba(127, 29, 29, 0.94), which is --danger-ink at 94%.
TableHistory.razor's .history-confirm is the fifth copy of the exact pair Slice 34 removed from four .chip-warn rules: 
#fdecea against --danger-surface 
#fbeaea, 
#f5c2c0 against --danger-hairline 
#f0c7c7. F-66's sweep missed it because it was looking at administration and this is a guest page — and it is the one panel in the guest area whose entire job is to look alarming before an irreversible action.
EventExplorer's five badge colours are all near-copies, not exact ones: a near-black that isn't --ink, a neutral tint that isn't --chip-surface, three role tints a few bits off the danger/accent/caution surfaces. That's the harder half — an exact copy is a duplicate, a near copy is a decision nobody made.
23 had no property to reach for at all, which is why the rest drifted: once literals were normal in a block, the ones that did have properties got written as literals too.
F-64's gate cannot see any of this. It asserts that every property a rule reads is declared. A rule that reads nothing and writes 
#b45309 is invisible to it — same wrong-palette failure, direction reversed.

F-69 — the fallback count stated in four documents was falsified by the slice that re-asserted it. §11.12, §16.4, F-64's ledger row and MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md all say "over a hundred references across sixteen components". Actual: 50 across 7. Slice 34 emptied four blocks, which is what removed them, and copied the number forward unchanged. F-50/F-62's shape exactly.

Work already completed in the sandbox
app.css :root rebuilt with 10 new properties (--accent-ink, --accent-surface, --accent-surface-soft, --accent-hairline, --caution-surface, --caution-ink-strong, --danger-signal, --danger-veil, --shadow-panel, --shadow-footer), each with the reasoning beside it.
All 45 literals converted; all 50 fallbacks stripped. Verified: 0 literals outside :root, 0 fallbacks, 14 blocks scanned, 329 var() references remaining.
Decision comments written beside every rule whose rendered colour changes (7 rules — I have the exact list).
One deliberate touch: the tree now contains a CSS comment naming var(--hairline, #e2e6ec) in prose, which fires 14 literals and 1 fallback if the new gate forgets to strip CSS comments and zero if it remembers — F-67's lesson made self-detecting rather than asserted.
What remains, and what I need from you
Still to write: the eighth [Fact] in HandheldLayoutContractTests.cs, and then TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (§11.12, §16.4, Appendix A rows F-68/F-69, v1.20 changelog — header and entry move together per F-48), DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md (full file), MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, _CHANGES.md. Then static analysis and the .tar.gz.

Two things worth your veto before I finish:

Seven rules change colour on screen. Byte-identical substitutions change nothing, but the drifted and near-copy ones do: the guest's hide warning, /kitchen's eighty-sixed row, the counter's settle confirmation, and all five EventExplorer badges. This follows F-66's precedent, but it's a visible change on live screens and it's a judgement, not a correction.
.sitting-meta stays open. It's declared by both ManageSitting (with margin: 0.2rem 0 0) and TableArea (without) — a drifted two-copy duplicate of a name app.css doesn't own. I edited TableArea for fallbacks and deliberately did not fix it, because resolving it means deciding whether the name is shared (→ app.css plus a prefix-list entry) or private (→ a rename touching markup), and neither belongs in a slice whose subject is colour. Where things stand
Slice 35 is substantially built and verified in the sandbox. It turned out to be three findings, not two — the third came out of reconciling Slice 34's test-count prediction against your terminal log.

The three findings
F-68 — the palette is written back into the tree as literals, and seven copies had already drifted.
95 colour values sit outside :root. Of the 45 bare ones, 20 are byte-identical to a declared property — 
#ffffff six times against --surface-raised (three of them inside app.css itself), 
#b45309 five times against --caution-ink, plus rgba(22, 32, 43, α) three times, which is --ink in decimal and the one form no scan for #hex could ever have found. TableHistory's irreversible-hide warning drew 
#fdecea/
#f5c2c0 against the palette's 
#fbeaea/
#f0c7c7 — the exact pair Slice 34 removed from four .chip-warn copies, surviving in a fifth place because that sweep was looking at administration and this is a guest page. EventExplorer's five badge tints were near-copies, which is the harder half. F-64's gate cannot see any of it: it asks whether a name a rule reads is declared, and a rule that reads nothing and writes 
#b45309 is invisible to it.

F-69 — four documents stated a count of the tree that the slice re-asserting it had already falsified. §11.12, §16.4, F-64's ledger row and the plan all said "over a hundred, across sixteen components." Actual: fifty, across seven. Slice 34 emptied nine of the sixteen blocks and copied the number forward. The count was the entire argument for the rule being a should.

F-70 — a blocking gate landed in the tree and no document in this repository knew it existed. HandheldLayoutContractTests held eight [Fact] methods; §16.4 said Seven assertions; the class's own summary said seven facts; no ledger row, no changelog entry, no _CHANGES.md line. The eighth is OverflowWrapIsDeclaredExactlyOnceOnTheBodyElement — a good rule, arriving from outside the slice discipline (the dump's commit message is "add changes with gemini pro extended"). And your own arithmetic announced it: Slice 34 predicted 1077, the run returned 1078. One unexplained test was one undocumented gate, sitting in the log for a slice.

What's done and verified
app.css :root rebuilt: 10 new properties, each with its reasoning. All 45 literals converted, all 50 fallbacks stripped across 7 components.
All nine facts ported to Python and run: 9/9 pass on the delivered tree; 2 fail on the pre-slice tree (50 fallbacks, 95 literals) — before-and-after rather than a claim.
Nine must-report plants all report, including a colour planted inside the breakpoint query (proves the nested at-rule is read). Four must-not-report plants all pass: an id selector opening with six hex characters, background-color: transparent, a CSS comment naming both a hex literal and a var(--x, #hex) fallback, and the undamaged control. That last one is deliberately left in the tree so a future version of the fact that forgot to strip CSS comments fails on arrival rather than bounding its own reach the way F-67 did.
New TestingSectionContractTests.cs — reads §16.4, resolves every cited *Tests.cs by filename in both citation forms, compares each stated count. Proven sensitive by the tree itself with nothing planted: 8 of 9 agreed, the ninth was the handheld test. After the edits: 9 pairs, 0 disagreements.
